text:
Olivia: Hey y'all, ACME procurement asked if we can take a PO for the POC (they prefer net30) and want a delegated signer on the order form. They also asked for a pricing floor/ceiling clause for the trial. Any legal/security blockers? :wave:

Rahul: @Olivia Legal ok with PO for POC but we need clear delegation language and a delegation attestation. No open-ended SLA liability for trials. Recommend a capped credit and a monthly cap tied to fees paid.

Tess: Security: POC must be scoped to non-prod test data, no external dataset ingestion, and access limited to engineering/test accounts. If ACME needs log access we need an NDA + subprocessor note.

Leo: Engineering: we can carve a POC config that limits throughput and model features to control cost (e.g., 512 token max, disabled streaming, quantized variant). That should satisfy a pricing ceiling ask.

Anne: Finance: we can accept a PO. Requirements: PO number on invoice, billing contact, and whether net30 or net45. For delegated signer: procurement can supply a signed delegation or include the signature block on PO.

Olivia: Can someone propose concise order-form snippets for (1) SLA credit cap for POC, (2) delegation snippet, and (3) pricing floor/ceiling options we can present? I want to send this to procurement now.

Rahul: Draft SLA credit clause: "For the POC term, Redwood will target 99% availability. If monthly availability falls below 99%, Customer may claim a credit equal to the lesser of (i) 20% of that month's POC Fees or (ii) $7,500, not to exceed the Fees paid for that month." Keep it simple.

Rahul: Draft delegation language: "Delegation: Customer warrants that the person executing the PO or Order Form is authorized to sign for the Customer for POC-level purchases. Procurement may supply a delegation letter or an executed PO with signer name, title, and email; Redwood may rely on either as binding."

Tess: Security addendum line: "POC Data Scope: Test/non-production data only. No external dataset uploads or production data ingestion. Subprocessors as of execution attached in Appendix A. Any additional access requires prior written approval."

Leo: Pricing options to offer ACME (pick one):
  1) Floor: $6,000 minimum for POC month; Ceiling: per-unit price capped at $0.008/token.
  2) No floor, but a monthly spend cap of $12,000 enforced by config (512 tokens, limited concurrency).
  3) Hybrid: $3,000 floor + per-unit ceiling $0.01/token.

FinanceBot: Invoice draft created: INV-ACME-PO-789 for $6,000 (placeholder). Update when PO number received. Link: https://billing.redwood.ai/inv/INV-ACME-PO-789

Olivia: Nice. @Rahul can you make the SLA credit slightly more conservative to reflect POC risk? Maybe 15% / $5k cap? Procurement might push.

Rahul: Updated: "Customer may claim a credit equal to the lesser of (i) 15% of that month's POC Fees or (ii) $5,000, and in all events no more than the Fees paid for that month."

Anne: Also confirm: do we need an explicit indemnity carveout for POC? Legal: minimal indemnity language only; no unusual obligations for trials.

Tess: I'll add the subprocessors list and confirm no special controls are required for this POC. If ACME needs SOC2 evidence point them to our security package link.

Olivia: Great. Action items: @Rahul finalize redline, @Tess attach subproc + security package, @Leo lock POC routing/limits, @Anne confirm billing/net terms and wait for PO. I'll ping procurement with the three pricing options and the updated clauses.

Anne: :thumbsup:

Rahul: Uploading redline in ~45m — will post Drive link here.

Leo: I'll push `acme-poc-lite` config (512 token / 2 concurrency) and post the snippet once live.

Olivia: Thanks team — looping in procurement@acme.com, please confirm PO number, delegated signer name/email/title, and preferred pricing option (1/2/3).
